method: Rebuilt the Enschede study-unit buckets directly from current EER Table 1 and reconsidered progression, route-specific sensor work and the final project before checking the exact UCR schedules, current workbook contributions and reader fields.
findings: The EEMCS Creative Technology EER 2026–2027, section B Article 1.2 Table 1, establishes the English-taught Enschede route. Modules 1–4 and 5–8 total 60 EC each year. Smart Technology is selected for module five as the first of the officially ordered eligible specialisations, independently of UCR overlap. Interactive Media is also at UT and Humane by Design is taught at VU. Table 1 identifies the route-specific 2.5 EC module-eight choice as Sensor Technology in Sports. Year three contains 30 EC open minor or exchange and 30 EC graduation. The graduation semester includes 5 EC Academic Writing, 5 EC Reflection and 20 EC individual design and research (5 EC GP I and 15 EC GP II). The 12 display components preserve coherent modules while the study-unit list records underlying content and weights.

EER B1.8 requires 60 year-one and 30 year-two EC before minor study. Module 11 non-project study units require 60 year-one and 45 year-two EC. Graduation Project normally requires all 120 EC of modules 1–8, with limited pending-result and dispensation provisions. The second project part follows completion of the first. The EER also bars concurrent major projects across modules. The standard sequential route satisfies these conditions. The minor is genuine approved space with restrictions on internships, external courses, overlap and project participation. The final design assignment uses a public presentation and defence.

The smart option uses actual signal analysis and computational robotics, while sensor work, circuits and installation projects remain distinct. Creative Communication Laboratory supports a limited relationship with Art, Impact and Technology through deliberate artistic choices and audience experience. Consumer Product Design supports a direct but bounded relationship with Interaction Design through user needs, prototyping and iterative testing. Qualitative and empirical methods support the human option without claiming the full UX studio. The official project is individual and compulsory; the 15 EC optional UCR element is outside each planned 180 EC.
